read.ko: 우리는 누구와 점심을 먹을지부터 어떤 진로를 추구할지까지, 삶에서 많은 개인적인 선택을 한다.
read.en: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue.

read.ko: 그러나 우리가 집단으로서 결정을 내려야 하는 상황도 많다.
read.en: However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group.

read.ko: 집단 의사 결정은 서로 다른 의견을 지닌 수많은 목소리가 관여하기 때문에 개인적인 선택만큼 단순하지 않다.
read.en: Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions.

read.ko: 투표는 집단의 결정을 더 공정하고 더 효율적으로 만들기 위해 흔히 사용되며, 시간이 흐르면서 다양한 투표 방식이 개발되어 왔다.
read.en: Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time.

read.ko: 다음 이야기는 이러한 서로 다른 투표 방식이 어떻게 작동하는지를 보여 준다.
read.en: The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work.

read.ko: Greenville 고등학교 학생회 구성원들은 어려움에 처한 아이들을 위해 어떻게 돈을 모금할지 결정해야 했다.
read.en: The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need.

read.ko: 그들의 세 가지 선택지는 미술 전시회, 빵 바자회, 자선 콘서트였지만, 의견이 엇갈렸다.
read.en: Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions.

read.ko: 그래서 그들은 그것을 투표에 부치기로 했다.
read.en: So they decided to put it to a vote.

read.ko: 그들이 학생회 지도 교사인 Akers 선생님께 조언을 구하자, 선생님은 익숙한 투표 방식을 쓰지 말고 대신 다른 것을 시도해 보라고 권했다.
read.en: When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead.

read.ko: 조사를 좀 한 뒤, 학생회 구성원들은 단순 다수결(FPTP) 방식, 대안 투표(AV) 방식, 콩도르세 방식이라는 세 가지 다른 투표 제도를 시도해 보기로 했다.
read.en: After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method.

read.ko: 학생회 전체는 서로 다른 방식이 서로 다른 결과를 낼지 알아내고 싶어 했다.
read.en: The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.

read.ko: 투표 당일, 가능한 각 행사에 글자가 하나씩 주어졌다. ʻ미술 전시회’는 글자 A로 표시되었고, 글자 B는 ʻ빵 바자회’를 나타냈으며, C는 ʻ자선 콘서트’를 뜻했다.

read.en: Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference.

read.en: Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins.

para.en: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work. The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote. When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results.

On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.” Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA. After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows: [표 · 선호 순서별 득표] ABC 4 · ACB 1 · BAC 6 · BCA 1 · CAB 6 · CBA 2 (총 20표) The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.

Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.

Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C. Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner. The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.

Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method. After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others. Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience. It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.

Ms. Akers had previously used the alternative vote method in her own classes.

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 그것은 서로 다른 의견을 가진 수많은 목소리를 수반한다 해설: ‘다른 의견을 가진 수많은 목소리’는 실제 소리가 아니라 각자 자기 견해를 지닌 많은 사람이 결정에 참여한다는 뜻 → 그래서 개인적 선택만큼 간단하지 않음. ②voices를 문자 그대로(큰 목소리) 해석한 오답 ③한 명이 결정하면 여러 목소리가 관여하지 않음 ④설득·연설 언급 없음 ⑤의견이 갈려 예측이 어렵다 는 흐름과 반대. ① 사람들은 설득력 있는 연설을 들은 후 종종 마음을 바꾼다 ② 대개 한 명의 지도자가 모두를 대신하여 최종 결정을 내린다 ③ 집단 구성원들은 서로 논쟁할 때 큰 소리로 말하는 경향이 있다 ④ 많은 참여자가 관여하며, 각자 다른 사람들의 견해와 충돌할 수 있는 개인적 견해를 가지고 온다 ⑤ 누군가 말하기도 전에 집단이 어떻게 결정할지 예측하는 것이 가능하다

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) straightforward — (B) drawback — (C) broad
(A) straightforward — (B) advantage — (C) broad
(A) intricate — (B) advantage — (C) minimal
(A) intricate — (B) drawback — (C) broad

choice.ex: (A) straightforward (B) drawback (C) broad 근거 ❶❸❼❽ 해설: (A) ❶ the simplest of the three methods·❼ uncomplicated and easy to understand = 간단한 / (B) ❼ but it has a significant weakness = 결점 / (C) ❽ without the support of the majority = 폭넓은(과반수의) 지지 없이. intricate는 simplest와 반대, advantage는 weakness와 반대, minimal은 “최소한의 지지도 없이 이긴다”가 되어 1지망 최다 득표로 이긴다는 ❷와 모순. 요약문 해석: FPTP 방식은 투표자의 1순위 선택만 세기 때문에 세 가지 방식 중 가장 (A) 간단하다. 하지만 이러한 단순함에는 심각한 (B) 결점이 따른다. 즉, 한 선택지가 투표자들로부터 (C) 폭넓은 지지를 얻지 않고도 승자로 선언될 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. ❷ Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. ❸ Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. ❹ This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. ❺ The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. ❻ This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. ❼ The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. ❽ It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. ❾ That was the case here. ❿ According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. ⓫ However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.
choice.body: Because the FPTP method counts only voters’ top choices, it is the most (A)________ of the three methods. However, this simplicity comes with a serious (B)________: an option can be declared the winner without gaining (C)________ backing from the voters.

choice.body: In the student council’s vote, the charity concert won because it received the (A)________ number of first-preference votes. Yet these votes made up less than half of the total, which means the concert lacked the (B)________ of most members, who (C)________ other options as their first choice.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: The FPTP method is widely adopted when people in many countries choose their leaders.
Twelve council members ranked an option other than the charity concert first.
Under FPTP, a voter’s second and third choices have no effect on the outcome.
Most council members later expressed dissatisfaction with the result of the vote.
Option A received the fewest first-preference votes among the three options.
choice.ex: 본문은 콘서트가 과반수의 1지망 지지를 받지 못했다는 사실(⓫)만 말할 뿐, 구성원들이 결과에 불만을 표했다는 내용은 없음. 나머지 는 ❸ / ❻ / ❻⓫(20−8=12) / ❹에서 확인·추론 가능. ① 근거 ❹ — FPTP 방식은 많은 나라의 사람들이 지도자를 선출할 때 널리 채택된다. ② 근거 ❻⓫ — 12명의 자치회 구성원이 자선 콘서트가 아닌 다른 선택지를 1순위로 꼽았다. ③ 근거 ❸ — FPTP에서는 투표자의 2순위와 3순위 선택이 결과에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않는다. ④ 근거 없음(정답) — 대부분의 자치회 구성원은 나중에 투표 결과에 불만을 표했다. ⑤ 근거 ❻ — 선택지 A는 세 선택지 중 가장 적은 1지망 표를 받았다.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Option B would have won if the council had counted the votes once more
The second and third preferences decided the final outcome of the vote
The FPTP method was too complicated for the council to apply correctly
The council members unanimously agreed that the charity concert was the best choice
The charity concert won even though most council members preferred other options
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 이것이 바로 이 경우에 해당했다. 해설: 밑줄의 That은 ❽ “과반수의 지지 없이 투표에서 이기는 것”을 가리키고, here는 학생 자치회 투표를 가리킴. ⓫ 20명 중 8명(40%)만 콘서트를 1지망으 로 고름 → 대부분은 다른 선택지를 선호. ②만장일치는 40% 지지와 모순 ③❼ uncomplicated and easy to understand와 반대 ④❸ 2·3지망은 무시됨 ⑤ 재집계 언급 없음. ① 자치회가 표를 한 번 더 셌다면 선택지 B가 이겼을 것이다 ② 2지망과 3지망이 투표의 최종 결과를 결정했다 ③ FPTP 방식은 자치회가 올바르게 적용하기에 너무 복잡했다 ④ 자치회 구성원들은 자선 콘서트가 최선의 선택이라는 데 만장일치로 동의했다 ⑤ 대부분의 자치회 구성원이 다른 선택지를 선호했는데도 자선 콘서트가 이겼다
choice.body: It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert.

opt: (A) majority — (B) reallocates — (C) limited
(A) minority — (B) reallocates — (C) excessive
(A) majority — (B) discards — (C) excessive
(A) majority — (B) reallocates — (C) excessive
(A) minority — (B) discards — (C) limited
choice.ex: (A) majority (B) reallocates (C) excessive 근거 ❸❻❾⓫ 해설: (A) ❸ more than 50% of the first-preference votes = 과반 / (B) ❻ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences = 재배 분하다 / (C) ⓫ second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes = 과도한 영향력. minority는 50% 초과 조건과 반대, discards는 표를 버리는 것이라 재분배와 반대, limited는 ⓫ greater influence와 반대. 요약문 해석: 어떤 선택지도 1순위 표의 (A) 과반을 얻지 못하면, AV 방식은 가장 약한 선택지를 제거하고 투표자들의 다음 선호에 따라 그 표를 (B) 재배분한다. 이 과정은 승자를 빵 바자회로 바꾸었지만, 그것은 2순위 선택에 (C) 과도한 영향력을 줄 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. ❷ The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. ❸ For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. ❹ As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. ❺ Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. ❻ Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. ❼ As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. ❽ This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. ❾ As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. ❿ Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. ⓫ It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. ⓬ In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.
choice.body: When no option wins a (A)________ of first-choice votes, the AV method removes the weakest option and (B)________ its ballots according to voters’ next preferences. This process changed the winner to the bake sale, but it can give second choices (C)________ influence.

choice.body: Since the art show had the fewest first-choice supporters, it was (A)________, and four of its five ballots moved to the bake sale. The bake sale thus (B)________ the charity concert, yet its victory was largely (C)________ second-choice votes.

opt: Most council members later agreed that the AV method was fairer than the earlier method.
Only five council members chose the art show as their top option.
